metadata.description: Knowledge graph of the Gilgamesh Epic extracted from the 1928 Campbell Thompson translation in cuneiform literary style. Captures the structural layout of the twelve cuneiform tablets, the principal deities, heroes, and humans, and reifies ten major narrative events as n-ary hyperedges. Every narrative edge carries a literal, completely unaltered cuneiform-translation text excerpt in its label field as empirical proof, preserving brackets, brackets-hyphen markers, and original em dashes.
metadata.source: R. Campbell Thompson, The Epic of Gilgamish (1928 translation from cuneiform)
metadata.extractor: Antigravity i2t agent, schema-compatible with yoheinakajima/instagraph + i2t hyperedge/reification extensions

attrs.method: washing her hands, then Aruru Finger’d some clay, on the desert she moulded (it)

edges.label: So when the goddess Aruru heard this, in her mind she imagined (Straightway, this) Concept of Anu, and, washing her hands, (then) Aruru Finger’d some clay, on the desert she moulded (it): (thus) on the desert Enkidu made she, a warrior

attrs.comeliness: girl, displaying her bosom, Shew’d him her comeliness

attrs.consequence: Failed his knees, and he slack d in his running... wisdom

edges.label: Six days, (aye) seven nights, with the courtesan-girl in his mating. Sated at length with her charms, he turn d his face to his cattle, O the gazelles, (how) they scamper’d away, as soon as they saw him!

attrs.action: barr d up the door with his foot

edges.label: Enkidu barr d up the door with his foot, (and) to Gilgamish entry— Would not concede: they grappled and snorted(?) like bulls, (and) the threshold Shatter’d: the (very) wall quiver’d as Gilgamish!, Enkidu grappled

attrs.fate: they cut off the head of Humbaba

attrs.aid: raised mighty winds: (yea), a great wind

edges.label: Wherefore against Humbaba he raised mighty winds: (yea), a great wind... Seizing "Humbaba’ before and behind, so that nor to go forwards, Nor to go back was he able: and then Humbaba surrender’d. ... they cut off the head of Humbaba.

attrs.scorn: unfolded endless list of her husbands

edges.label: Lady Ishtar espieth the beauty of Gilgamish: (saith she), “Gilgamish, come, be a bridegroom... What, then, will be my advantage, supposing’ I take thee in marriage? Thou 'rt but a back door "not" giving resistance to blast or to windstorm, Thou 'rt but a palace which dasheth the heroes "within it to pieces’

attrs.insult: Wrenching the member from out of the Bull, he toss’d (it) before her

attrs.fight: Seized on the Heavenly Bull by ‘his’ horns

attrs.wail: mounted Ishtar (the crest of) the ramparts of Erech

attrs.offering: its heart they removed, Unto the Sun-god they offer'd

edges.label: (So), what time they the Bull of the Heavens had kili’d, its heart they - removed, Unto the Sun-god they offer'd in sacrifice... Woe unto Gilgamish—he who by killing the Bull of the Heavens, Made me lament. ... Wrenching the member from out of the Bull, he toss’d (it) before her

attrs.dread: Sorrow hath enter’d my heart; I fear death

edges.label: Gilgamish bitterly wept for his comrade, (for) Enkidu, ranging Over the desert: "I, too—shall I not die like Enkidu also? Sorrow hath enter’d my heart; I fear death as I range o’er the desert, I will get hence on the road to the presence of Uta-Napishtim

attrs.revelation: conspirator with them, Unto a reed-hut their counsel betray’d

edges.label: Nin-igi-azag— tis Ea—, (albeit) conspirator with them, Unto a reed-hut their counsel betray’d he: "O Reed-hut, O Reed-hut ! Wall, wall! Hearken, O Reed-hut, consider, O Wall! ... Six days, al se’nnight the hurricane, deluge, (and) tempest continued

attrs.loss: Then Gilgamish sate him, (and) burst into weeping

edges.label: There is a plant like a thorn... Bound heavy stones "on his feet?, which dragg’d him down... a serpent who snuff'd the plant's fragrance... snatch’d the plant... Then Gilgamish sate him, (and) burst into weeping.

attrs.wisdom: spirit of Enkidu issued Forth like a wind

attrs.plea: Spake he: O Nergal... Ope now, a hole

edges.label: Oped, then, a hole in the earth, and the spirit of Enkidu issued Forth from the earth like a wind. They embraced and..... Communed together, mourning. ... What I have seen of the laws of the Underworld, —sit thee down weeping ! ”
